frame: base_link: the drone's body, FLU (x forward, y left, z up), origin at the Iris model's origin. Poses are translation [x, y, z] in metres and rotation [axis x, y, z, angle] (Webots axis-angle).

imu.name: imu
imu.model: TDK ICM-40609-D, inside the Mid-360: (11.0, 23.29, -44.12) mm in its point-cloud frame
imu.note: ICM-40609-D datasheet (TDK DS-000330): white noise is its total RMS noise over 100 Hz (0.045 deg/s, 1.0 mg; rad/s, m/s^2 per sample); bias, scale and cross-axis are its initial tolerances (+-1 deg/s, +-40 mg, +-0.5%, +-1%), each drawn once from the seed, uniformly within them: one unit, the same every run. Not modelled: temperature drift (constant temperature), bias random walk (not specified). The Mid-360 publishes 200 Hz; 250 Hz is the nearest rate a 2 ms physics step can sample. ArduPilot keeps the Iris's own noiseless accelerometer, gyro, inertial unit and GPS (truth), adding its own noise in SITL.

lidar.name: lidar
lidar.model: Livox Mid-360: 200,000 points/s on 4 lines, 360 degrees, 0.1 to 40 m at 10% reflectivity, range precision 2 cm, angular precision 0.15 deg
lidar.note: pattern: fitted by tools/fit_mid360_pattern.py to a real Mid-360's recording (outdoor_kidnap_a, Hard Point Cloud Localization Dataset, Zenodo 10122133, CC BY 4.0): over 203 s, residuals 1.8 deg (elevation, median) and 1.7 deg (the fan's azimuth, RMS); it covers -7.0 to 51.9 deg. The render: 0.1 deg pixels over +-52.3 deg, rows as many as Webots' image (so none is skipped). reflectivity: every surface's, forest at 905 nm (foliage 0.4-0.5, bark and soil 0.2-0.3). Not modelled: beam footprint (edges are sharp, no mixed returns), range accuracy (+-3 cm) beyond precision, returns past the render's 40 m (the datasheet's 70 m at 80%).
